title: Developer Graph — Technology Foundation for Social Collaboration Fabric
context: ADR 016 defined the sandbox Cell model. The next layer is the Developer Graph — the pseudo-social layer where people and Cells discover each other, establish trust, form work contexts, and route collaboration. This is not a social network. It is a social collaboration fabric for executable projects. The network can route attention and proposals, but it cannot mutate local truth. This ADR imports the shared authority spine so the graph remains a projection over durable events rather than a competing truth source. Deep research (June 2026) validated all major technology choices against the 2026 landscape: AT Protocol DIDs proven at 43M+ Bluesky user scale, W3C DID v1.1 at Candidate Rec, UCAN spec stable at v1.0.0-rc.1, Yjs dominant at 920K weekly downloads with Yrs Rust rewrite, and event sourcing with PGlite as established PostgreSQL event store pattern.
decision:
### Technology Stack

Deep research (June 2026) validates all technology choices:

**AT Protocol (Bluesky):** 43M+ users, Sync 1.1 relay cost $20-30/mo, active Rust rewrite (atproto-space, atproto-pds crates). New Spaces concept for permissioned records. Signed data repositories with Merkle Search Trees, IPLD dag-cbor, CID hashes. Lexicon schemas for global interoperability. XRPC (HTTP-with-conventions). PDS uses SQLite + Litestream. Architecture separates speech (PDS) from reach (Relays/App Views). IETF standardization ongoing.

**DIDs (Decentralized Identifiers):** W3C DID v1.1 Candidate Recommendation Snapshot (April 2026). 45M+ active DIDs, 15% monthly growth. Market projected $7.4B in 2026. EU eIDAS 2.0 mandating decentralized identity wallets from Jan 2026. did:plc (Bluesky, rotation keys for PDS migration) and did:web (simple, DNS trust roots). BBS+ signature standard for privacy-preserving batch credential presentation.

**UCAN:** v1.0.0-rc.1 stable, pure delegation model running on hashes of CIDs. Proof chains with delegation, capability scoping, DID principals. UCAN Invocation v1.0.0-rc.1 defines the final 'use' step. Complementary to OAuth (authentication) vs UCAN (authorization). UCAN Working Group at IETF.

**Yjs (CRDT):** 920K weekly NPM downloads, authoritative collaborative editing CRDT. Network-agnostic, offline-capable, version snapshots, undo/redo. Yrs (Rust rewrite) for performance. Dominant ecosystem: Liveblocks, PartyKit, most collaboration tools. Automerge v2 as alternative with per-document CRDT approach.

**Event Sourcing:** Append-only event logs with monotonic sequence, actor DID, event type, timestamp, payload JSON, hash, previous hash. CQRS read model projections. PGlite event tables as canonical store. JSONL as export/envelope format.

### Three Layers

Layer 1 - Cell-native graph: authoritative for Tribunus collaboration. Envelopes, receipts, capability grants, sandbox proposals. Stored in PGlite event tables. Layer 2 - Public protocol adapters: ATProto-compatible PDS adapter (optional), Nostr relay adapter (optional discovery), ActivityPub adapter (optional fediverse). Layer 3 - Social UX: profiles, project cards, follow graph, feeds, work signals, sandbox entry points. The graph remains a projection layer over durable events, not a source of runtime authority.

### Portable Identity

AT Protocol DIDs via Bluesky: did:plc or did:web for users. GitHub OAuth bootstraps initial DID mapping. No new account creation required.

### Capability-Based Access

UCAN scoped authority: User X can participate in sandbox S for project P with scope (read code, run tests, propose changes) with constraints (files in /src/** only, 60-minute session) with delegation (may invite others with subset of scope). MVP ships with OAuth session grants internally modeled as capability grants with UCAN-compatible shape. Full UCAN proof chains for shareable/offline invite links.
consequences:
### Positive

Portable identity from day one (AT Protocol DIDs mean no vendor lock-in). Event-sourced graph is auditable (every connection, proposal, review is immutable event). UCAN scoped authority matches Cell model (capability-based access control, offline-first verification, delegation without key sharing). Interoperability with Atmosphere (tens-of-millions-scale Bluesky ecosystem validates portable identity). No external protocol dependency for core operation (graph is native). Yjs 920K/wk downloads validates CRDT choice.

### Negative

AT Protocol still standardizing (IETF process underway, Spaces concept in development). UCAN less mature than OAuth (v1.0.0-rc.1 stable but less widely deployed than OAuth 2.1). Event-sourced projections add maintenance overhead (read model rebuild, eventual consistency). GitHub OAuth bootstrap retains centralized trust root.

### Risk: AT Protocol Standardization

IETF process is editorial/structural only — protocol is de facto stable at 43M+ scale. Mitigation: Cell-native graph uses internal envelope format; ATProto is a public-facing adapter, not the backbone. Adapters can be replaced without core architecture changes.

### Risk: UCAN Maturity

v1.0.0-rc.1 stable but ecosystem smaller than OAuth. Mitigation: MVP uses OAuth session grants in UCAN-compatible shape.

### Risk: Projection Maintenance

CQRS read models require sync between event log and projections. Mitigation: rebuild projections from event log on restart.
